question.prompt: What is the least possible value of \((xy - 1)^2 + (x + y)^2\) for real numbers \(x\) and \(y?\)

solutions.title: Cancel the mixed terms and factor
solutions.explanation:
Expanding the two squares makes the mixed terms cancel, revealing a useful product:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(xy-1)^2+(x+y)^2
&=x^2y^2-2xy+1+x^2+2xy+y^2\\
&=x^2y^2+x^2+y^2+1\\
&=(x^2+1)(y^2+1).
\end{aligned}
\]
For real \(x,y\), both squares are nonnegative, so each factor is at least \(1\). Their product is therefore at least \(1\).

When \(x=y=0\), both factors equal \(1\), so this bound is attained. The least possible value is \(\boxed{1}\), choice \(\text{D}\).

solutions.title: Expand and retain nonnegative square terms
